newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes up, helped by weaker dollar.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes up, helped by weaker dollar.

text.p: Gold prices whipped through a range of over a dollar in early European trading on Wednesday as several factors converged to move the market, dealers said.
"The stock market and the dollar are both weaker and there has been some producer selling," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $369.60 per ounce after $368.25 on Tuesday afternoon and a close of $368.50/$369.00.

Far East markets were slightly firmer from the previous London close as they consolidated after gold fell to three-year lows last week. Any upward momentum was restrained by talk of Russian selling and forward sales by Australian miners.
Dealers said the market was caught slightly off guard by the 0.50 percentage point cut in Australian interest rates to six percent.

The cut, the third in five months, reflected a further improvement in the domestic inflation outlook. Inflation was likely to remain below 2.5 percent, according to an Australian central bank official.
"The Australians have been selling since their rate cut and there has been talk of South African producers selling too," one dealer said.
With operations already beginning to wind down ahead of the Christmas holiday and the approach of year-end, the market was likely to remain fairly thin and nervous, a dealer said.
However, gold appeared to have found a base in the past couple of days after slipping to its lowest price in three years last week at $366.00.
"Support looks to be available at $368.00 so people are fairly happy to stay a bit long for the moment," a dealer said.
A break through $370.50 could lead gold up to $373.00, he added. Other dealers felt that level, if attained, would be the high for the rest of the year.
Silver was marked up about four cents from the previous close to $4.84/$4.86, but the market was thin, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium were also fairly quiet. Platinum appeared to be under less pressure than it had been recently, but the price remained at a discount to gold.
It was indicated at $369.00/$370.00, up $1.50 from the previous close, but palladium was $0.25 easier at $118.00/$119.00.
